 Court No. - 84
 Hon'Ble Subhash Chandra Sharma, J. 
1.

This criminal appeal has been preferred against the judgment and order dated 26.04.1983 passed by VII Additional Sessions Judge, Meerut in Session Trial No. 239 of 1980, under Section 366, 342 I.P.C., Police Station Khekra, District Meerut (State Vs. Shahbuddin and Samaidin) arising out of Crime No. 60 of 1979 by which learned court concerned has convicted and sentenced the appellants under sections 366, 342 for four years rigorous imprisonment.

entities.text: Police Station Khekra, District Meerut (State Vs. Shahbuddin and Samaidin
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. Prosecution case in brief is that the informant Kehar Singh lodged an F.I.R. on 20.03.1979 at about 17:20 P.M. that his daughter Urmila was missing.

At this S.I. O.P. Bhati, Constable Rampal Singh, Constable Bathuwa Singh went to the village in the house of appellant Shahbuddin and his brother Samaidin and made search in their house on the basis of suspicion from where the victim was recovery, as a result present F.I.R. was lodged.

3. After investigation of the case charge sheet was filed against the appellants under Sections 366,
376, 342 IPC.
4.
The learned court concerned, took cognizance of the offences and after complying with the provisions of Section 207 Cr.P.C, committed the case to the Court of Sessions for trial.
5. The learned trial court framed the charge under Sections 366 and 342 IPC against the appellants on the basis of material on record which was read-over and explained to the appellants.
They did not plead guilty but claimed for trial.
6. After conclusion of prosecution evidence statement of appellants under Section 313 Cr.P.C. were recorded in which they stated the incident to be false and witnesses to be inimical.

In Defence DW 1,
Jeet Singh; DW 2 Chottan were examined at length.
7. After hearing the arguments for accused/appellants as well as the State, the learned trial court passed the impugned judgment dated 26.04.1983.
8. Being aggrieved with the conviction and sentence, this criminal appeal has been preferred by the appellants against the order of the learned trial court.

9. Heard learned counsel for the appellants as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
10.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that they are innocent and have falsely been implicated in this case.

He further submits that in this case the incident is said to have taken place Shahbuddin And Another vs State Of U.P. on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14719933/
2 on 19.03.1979 and judgment was passed by the learned trial court in the year 1983.

entities.text: Shahbuddin And Another vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Till now 46 years have elapsed and the appellant Samaidin has become aged about more than 67 years and appellant Shahbuddin more than 60 years.
He further submits that during trial, after conviction and during the pendency of this appeal they have served the sentence for a period of 64 days in jail.
Now, they are in jail in pursuance to the N.B.W. issued by this Court.
He also submits that since the incident took place prior to 46 years from today and at that time the appellants were in the tender age and now they have become old.
No purpose will be served by sending him to jail, therefore, they be released on the period they have undergone in jail and some fine may be imposed as compensation to be paid to the victim.

11. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the contentions made by learned counsel for the appellants but could not dispute the fact about time gap from the date of incident till now and the age of the appellants.
12. Before dealing with the contentions raised by learned counsel for the appellants, it will be convenient to take note of the evidences as adduced by the prosecution.

13. In support of its case, prosecution examined, P.W.1 Dr. Rajani Gupta; P.W.2 Constable Asarfi Lal; P.W. 3 Urmila (the victim); P.W. 4 Kehar Singh; P.W.5 S.I. O.P. Bhati,; P.W. 6 S.I. Balbir Singh Yadav.
14. In the case of Neelam Bahal & another v. State of Uttrakhand 2010 (2) SCC 229 where conviction and sentence of appellant u/s 307 IPC was converted into S.326 IPC simpliciter.

entities.text: Neelam Bahal & another v. State of Uttrakhand 2010 (2) SCC 229
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Incident took place in the year 1987 and appellant was about 25 years old.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, Hon'ble the Apex Court reduced the sentence to the period undergone by him.

Likewise, in the case of Hussainbhai Asgarali Lokhandwala v. State of Gujarat dated 14 August 2024 in Criminal Appeal No. 1691 of 2023 Hon'ble Apex Court modified to the period of incarceration already undergone by him while maintaining the conviction where the entire incident had occurred in the heat of moment on 07.11.2000.
15.

entities.text: Hussainbhai Asgarali Lokhandwala v. State of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the learned counsel for the appellants limits his argument to the extent of sentence and the period appellants remained in jail, therefore, the merit of the case is not to be interfered except the sentence.
From record it is evident that appellant no. 1 Shahbuddin was aged about 17 years and appellant no. 2 Samaidin was aged 25 years.
At the time of incident, both are real brothers now they are more than 67 and 60 years and are also suffering from old aged infirmities.
The incident took place in the year 1979 and till now 46 years have elapsed and they have served the sentence for a period of 64 days during the period of trial.

16. In considered opinion of this Court, keeping in view the aforesaid circumstances of the case and the observation made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the time gap & the age of appellants it will serve no purpose to send appellants to jail for serving out the remaining period of sentence, but it will be just and proper and will serve the purpose of justice to impose fine to be paid as compensation to the complainant/injured or his survivors.

17. Accordingly, this appeal is partly allowed and the sentence awarded against the appellant no. 1, Shahbuddin, appellant no. 2,
Shahbuddin And Another vs State Of U.P. on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14719933/
3 Samaidin is reduced to the period of sentence already undergone by them and they are to deposit Rs. 20,000/- proportionately before the concerned court within a period of 30 days from today which shall be paid either to the injured or their survivors.
